comparisons.peer_summary: AMD develops tailored, high-performance semi-custom solutions based on CPU, GPU, and multimedia technologies, powering major gaming consoles including the Sony PlayStation 5, Microsoft Xbox Series S/X, and Valve Steam Deck, with the PlayStation 5 Pro launching in 2024 featuring enhanced graphics and AI capabilities.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Micron highlight the role of AI capabilities in driving demand for their respective products within mobile and device ecosystems, though they focus on different segments: Micron focuses on memory capacity requirements for on-device AI in smartphones, while AMD focuses on the custom silicon powering specific gaming consoles with AI features. Micron states that 'Enabling these on-device AI capabilities is driving increased memory and storage capacity needs and increasing demand for new value-add solutions' in the context of smartphones. AMD notes that 'In 2024, Sony launched the PlayStation 5 Pro with additional graphics performance and AI capabilities compared to the original PlayStation 5,' linking AI to its semi-custom console products. Both disclosures identify AI as a key driver for new product iterations and performance enhancements in consumer devices.

sentences.text: Enabling these on-device AI capabilities is driving increased memory and storage capacity needs and increasing demand for new value-add solutions.
In 2024, Sony launched the PlayStation 5 Pro with additional graphics performance and AI capabilities compared to the original PlayStation 5.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company provides Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and GPS/GNSS solutions for mobile devices, including integrated combination chips and location platform services.
comparisons.comparison: Both Micron and Broadcom address the mobile device market, but Micron focuses on the memory and storage demand drivers (specifically AI) while Broadcom focuses on the connectivity infrastructure (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth) that enables mobile device functionality. Micron cites that 'The proliferation of smartphones, tablets, and other mobile devices continues to increase the demand for memory chips.' Broadcom describes its 'Connectivity Solutions' as including 'discrete and integrated Wi-Fi and Bluetooth solutions... designed for use in mobile devices including smartphones, tablets and wearable products.' While both companies serve the same end-market (smartphones/tablets), their specific product focus and demand drivers (memory vs. connectivity) are distinct components of the mobile ecosystem.

comparisons.peer_summary: Consumer IoT products are adopting latest mobile connectivity and on-device AI capabilities, with new AI-focused PCs launching in 2024 and analysts expecting 50% of PCs sold to be AI capable by 2027.
comparisons.comparison: Both Micron and Qualcomm identify on-device AI as a primary driver for increased demand for memory and storage in mobile devices, specifically citing smartphones and PCs. Micron states that 'Smartphones offer tremendous potential for personalized AI capabilities that offer greater security and responsiveness when executed on the device' and that this is 'driving increased memory and storage capacity needs.' Qualcomm echoes this by noting that 'Consumer IoT products, including personal computing (e.g., tablets and PCs)... continue to adopt the latest mobile connectivity, processing and intelligence technologies including on-device AI capabilities,' which 'enables new services... running directly on the device.' Both companies explicitly link the shift toward on-device AI processing to the necessity for enhanced device capabilities (memory for Micron, processing/connectivity for Qualcomm).

sentences.text: Smartphones offer tremendous potential for personalized AI capabilities that offer greater security and responsiveness when executed on the device.
Enabling these on-device AI capabilities is driving increased memory and storage capacity needs and increasing demand for new value-add solutions.

Consumer IoT products, including personal computing (e.g., tablets and PCs), voice and music and XR, continue to adopt the latest mobile connectivity, processing and intelligence technologies including on-device AI capabilities.
This enables new services, applications and experiences that can be run directly on the device, driving improvements in latency, cost and privacy.
